title: United South Celebrates 10 Years of Business Etiquette Training
excerpt: United South High School’s Academy of Global Business & Advanced Technology Magnet marked the 10th straight year of its Business Etiquette Seminar, with juniors practicing dining and conversation skills over lunch at El Paseo Real.
content:
United South High School celebrated the 10th consecutive year of its Business Etiquette Seminar, an annual tradition for juniors in the Academy of Global Business & Advanced Technology Magnet, the district announced.

This year’s seminar brought magnet juniors to El Paseo Real for hands-on training with Diane Gottsman, an etiquette expert from San Antonio and founder of The Protocol School of Texas, according to the district. The seminar is led by Dr. Sinneh J. Koroma, dean of the magnet academy.

Students worked through questions such as what to do if something spills during a business lunch and how to use a napkin, practicing professional dining and conversation skills over lunch with their classmates, the district said. The training prepares them for interviews, internships and other situations where a first impression matters.

“The value of this dining skills training is that it takes away the awkward moments that could arise at a professional meeting,” Gottsman said. “These students are young ambassadors looking for their next big opportunity.”

Gottsman said knowing what to do at the table lets students focus on the people they are meeting, and she encouraged them to put away their phones and give the person across from them their full attention, according to the district.

Koroma said one of the most rewarding parts comes afterward, when students talk about what they learned and how they would handle similar situations on their own. He described the takeaway as “confidence, preparation, and just knowing that I can do it.”

Gottsman, who usually works with university students and corporate groups, said she first agreed to lead the seminar after speaking with Koroma and hearing how committed he was to developing student leaders. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she recalled, students and their families picked up meals, drinks and desserts in their cars and joined the training online while she taught from the school library, according to the district.

Sources: United Independent School District, Nov. 19, 2026.
